subtopic: Schedule II and III quantity limits
stem: A buprenorphine prescription for opioid use disorder requests a 90-day single fill. Which Massachusetts quantity pathway is relevant?

choices.text: Use the out-of-state prescription rule when its schedule, age, and verification conditions have not been checked.
Process another refill because an authorization written by the prescriber overrides schedule limits.
Treat the request as an insufficient-stock partial fill and use the 72-hour remainder rule.
The Schedule III opioid-use-disorder treatment pathway may allow up to a 90-day single fill if no other restriction controls.
Handle the drug or transaction as ordinary Massachusetts Schedule VI activity.

explanation.core_reasoning: Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps. buprenorphine (Subutex) is used for treatment of opioid dependence. It is federal Schedule III and Massachusetts Schedule III; its legal consequence in this scenario follows the cited schedule-specific rule.

choice_analysis.C: That choice belongs, if at all, to Schedule II partial fill caused by pharmacy inability; its trigger does not match this scenario.
choice_analysis.D: This applies Massachusetts Schedule II and III single-fill quantity framework: Massachusetts generally limits Schedule II and III opioid prescriptions to a 30-day supply and recognizes defined 90-day pathways for OUD drugs, non-opioid Schedule II or III drugs, and implantable infusion pumps.
choice_analysis.E: That choice belongs, if at all, to Massachusetts Schedule VI prescription-drug status; its trigger does not match this scenario.
